title: LED-based characterization of solar cells for underwater applications
author: Zhang, Sartor, et al.

steps.title: Set up measurement hardware
steps.instruction: Place the LED solar simulator (e.g., Oriel VeraSol‑2) on the bench, connect a Keithley 2400 source‑measure unit and a laboratory PC, and mount the solar cell on an adjustable‑height lab jack positioned under the simulator.

steps.title: Prepare EQE data files
steps.instruction: Obtain the external quantum efficiency (EQE) spectra for the reference mc‑Si cell and the test device, save each as a CSV file with columns ‘wv’ (wavelength in nm) and ‘qe’ (EQE), ensuring identical wavelength ranges for both files.

steps.title: Run SpectraMaximus scripts
steps.instruction: Execute the provided Python code (SpectraMaximus) which (a) calculates LED power settings to reproduce the desired underwater attenuation spectrum, (b) computes the target short‑circuit current for the reference cell, (c) determines the spectral mismatch coefficient M, and (d) performs the current‑correction calculations.

substeps.instruction: Load LED output spectra, underwater spectra, AM1.5G reference spectrum, reference‑cell EQE and test‑cell EQE into the script.
Run the functions that implement Equations 3, 4‑5, 9‑10, and the correction workflow.

steps.title: Calibrate device‑simulator distance
steps.instruction: Using the adjustable lab jack, vary the distance between the solar cell and the LED simulator until the measured short‑circuit current of the calibrated reference cell satisfies Equation 3: IDUTLED / IDUTUW = 1.

steps.title: Calculate target short‑circuit current
steps.instruction: With SpectraMaximus, input the LED outputs, underwater spectrum, AM1.5G reference spectrum, reference‑cell EQE and test‑cell EQE; the script solves Equation 3 to give the target short‑circuit current I_DUT,LED at the calibrated height.

steps.title: Determine spectrum calibration numbers
steps.instruction: Compute the calibration numbers using Equations 4 and 5: CNUW = I_REF U W / E_UW, CNRC = I_REF R C / E_tot, then I_REF UW = I_REF RC × CN_UW × E_UW / (CN_RC × E_tot).

steps.title: Compute spectral mismatch coefficient
steps.instruction: Evaluate the integrals in Equation 9 and 10 to obtain M = (IDUTLED / IREFLED) × (IREFUW / IDUTUW) = [∫ε_LED·SR_DUT dλ / ∫ε_LED·SR_REF dλ] × [∫ε_UW·SR_REF dλ / ∫ε_UW·SR_DUT dλ].

steps.title: Convert EQE to spectral response
steps.instruction: For each EQE file, compute the spectral response SR(λ) using SR = (q λ / h c) EQE = λ / 1239.8 × EQE; implement the supplied Python loop to add a ‘sr’ column to the dataframe.

substeps.instruction: Read CSV with pandas: test = pd.read_csv(file, header=0, names=['wv','qe']).
If first file, store wavelength column in df_EQE.
Calculate sr = (test['qe']) * (test['wv'] / 1239.8) and append to dataframe.

steps.title: Isolate reference LED current
steps.instruction: Rearrange Equation 9 to solve for I_REFLED, giving I_REFLED = I_REFUW × M (Equation 12).

steps.title: Apply spectral mismatch correction
steps.instruction: Using the code fragment, interpolate the simulated spectrum, compute integrals int1‑int5 with np.trapz, calculate h = int3/int4, adjust simulated irradiance E_sim = E_sim/h, compute mismatch m = (int1/int2) × (int3/int4), then correct short‑circuit current: I_uw_ref = I_rc_ref × (int1/int5), I_sim_ref = I_uw_ref / m.
